options.label: A common name for many flowering cacti that bloom at night
options.feedback: Correct. It is a common name covering many different ceroid cacti that share the habit of opening at night.

options.label: A single species of cactus found only in deserts
options.feedback: Not that. Night-blooming cereus is a common name for many species, not one, and they are not all desert plants.

options.label: A type of flower that stays open for several nights
options.feedback: No. Most night-blooming cereus flowers open for just one night, and some for only part of it.

options.label: A plant that blooms during the day instead of at night
options.feedback: The name says otherwise. These cacti bloom at night, not during the day.

items.ok_line: It is a shared name for many night-blooming cacti.
items.ko_line: Remember it covers many species, not one.
items.exp_text: Night-blooming cereus is a common name applied to many flowering ceroid cacti that bloom at night. The name is not a single species but a label for a group of cacti sharing this habit.

items.prompt: How long does a single flower of Selenicereus grandiflorus stay open?

options.label: Several weeks
options.feedback: No. The plant may put out flowers over several weeks, but each individual flower only lasts a single night.

options.label: One night
options.feedback: Correct. The flower of Selenicereus grandiflorus opens for only one night.

options.label: One week
options.feedback: Not that. A week is far longer than the flower remains open; it is gone by dawn.

options.label: A whole day and night
options.feedback: No. It opens after nightfall and wilts by dawn, so it does not even last a full day.

items.ok_line: That flower opens and fades within one night.
items.ko_line: It is just one night, not weeks or days.
items.exp_text: Selenicereus grandiflorus produces flowers that each open for a single night. Although the plant may bloom multiple times over several weeks, every individual flower lives only that one night.

items.prompt: Which cactus is the most popular cultivated night-blooming cereus?

options.label: Selenicereus grandiflorus
options.feedback: Not that. Although it is a night-blooming cereus, it is not the most popular one grown; Epiphyllum oxypetalum holds that place.

options.label: Hylocereus undatus
options.feedback: No. That one is often grown outdoors for its fruit, but the most popular cultivated for its flowers is Epiphyllum oxypetalum.

options.label: Epiphyllum oxypetalum
options.feedback: Correct. Epiphyllum oxypetalum, also called gooseneck cactus, is the most popular cultivated night-blooming cereus and is grown as a houseplant worldwide.

options.label: Peniocereus greggii
options.feedback: No. That desert cactus is infrequently cultivated, not the most popular one.

items.ok_line: Epiphyllum oxypetalum is the top choice among growers.
items.ko_line: It is Epiphyllum oxypetalum, not the others.
items.exp_text: Among night-blooming cereus, Epiphyllum oxypetalum is the most popular cultivated one. It is grown as an indoor houseplant throughout the world because it is relatively easy to keep.

items.prompt: What colour are the flowers of night-blooming cereus almost always?

options.label: White or very pale shades of other colours
options.feedback: Correct. The flowers are almost always white or very pale, with large and often fragrant blooms.

options.label: Bright red or orange
options.feedback: No. Night-blooming cereus flowers are not brightly coloured; they are pale, usually white.

options.label: Deep purple or blue
options.feedback: That is not right. The flowers are pale, not deep or dark coloured.

options.label: Yellow with dark spots
options.feedback: No. The flowers are uniformly pale, almost always white, not spotted yellow.

items.ok_line: They are white or very pale in colour.
items.ko_line: The flowers are never bright or dark.
items.exp_text: The flowers of night-blooming cereus are almost always white or very pale shades of other colours. This pale colour is typical of flowers that open at night.

items.prompt: When does the flower of a night-blooming cereus usually open?

options.label: At noon
options.feedback: No. The flowers open after nightfall, not in the middle of the day.

options.label: Just before sunrise
options.feedback: Not that. Opening happens after dark, and by dawn the flowers are already wilting.

options.label: In the early afternoon
options.feedback: No. These are night-blooming flowers; they open after the sun has gone down.

options.label: After nightfall
options.feedback: Correct. Most of the flowers open after nightfall and are wilting by dawn.

items.ko_line: It is after nightfall, not during the day.
items.exp_text: Most night-blooming cereus flowers open after nightfall. By dawn, they are already wilting, so their open time is limited to the dark hours.

items.prompt: What happens to many night-blooming cereus flowers by dawn?

options.label: They open wider
options.feedback: No. By dawn they are wilting, not opening wider.

options.label: They are wilting
options.feedback: Correct. Most of the flowers are wilting by dawn, ending their short life.

options.label: They turn green
options.feedback: No. They do not change colour; they simply wilt.

options.label: They fall off the plant
options.feedback: Not exactly. They wilt but do not necessarily fall off immediately at dawn.

items.ok_line: The flowers wilt when morning comes.
items.ko_line: They wilt rather than stay fresh or open.
items.exp_text: By dawn, most night-blooming cereus flowers are wilting. Their opening at night is brief, and they do not last into the daylight.

items.prompt: What is the shape of most night-blooming cereus plants?

options.label: Short and bushy with many branches
options.feedback: No. Most are thin-stemmed climbers, not short bushes.

options.label: Round and ball-like
options.feedback: Not that. They are not round; they are tall columnar or thin climbing plants.

options.label: Thin-stemmed climbers
options.feedback: Correct. Most night-blooming cereus are thin-stemmed climbers, though some can be tall and columnar.

options.label: Flat and ground-hugging
options.feedback: No. They usually climb or grow tall, not hug the ground flat.

items.ko_line: They are climbers, not bushes or balls.
items.exp_text: Most night-blooming cereus plants are thin-stemmed climbers, although some are tall and columnar, sometimes extremely large and tree-like.

items.prompt: Which night-blooming cereus is best known and grows from an underground tuber?

options.label: Epiphyllum oxypetalum
options.feedback: No. That one is a popular houseplant, not the desert plant with a tuber.

options.label: Hylocereus undatus
options.feedback: Not that. Hylocereus undatus is grown for fruit, not known for an underground tuber.

options.label: Selenicereus grandiflorus
options.feedback: No. That is the single-night bloomer, not the tuber-growing desert cactus.

options.label: Peniocereus greggii
options.feedback: Correct. Peniocereus greggii is the best-known night-blooming cereus that grows from an underground tuber and lives strictly as a desert plant.

items.ok_line: Peniocereus greggii grows from a tuber.
items.ko_line: It is Peniocereus greggii, not the others.
items.exp_text: Peniocereus greggii is the best-known night-blooming cereus that is strictly a desert plant. It grows from an underground tuber and is infrequently cultivated.
